figures.caption: With only a KG and no question annotations, EoG lets an LLM self-evolve by proposing questions verified on the graph and then learning to solve them.

figures.label: fig:paradigm
figures.caption: Comparison of KG reasoning paradigms. Prompt-based agents explore with a frozen LLM and RL-based agents learn from fixed QA written by humans or closed-source models, whereas EoG proposes and solves KG-verified tasks of adaptive difficulty. With Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, EoG outperforms all shown baselines on three Freebase benchmarks.

figures.label: fig:framework
figures.caption: Overview of EoG. One LLM self-plays as the Proposer and the Solver, synthesizes verifiable tasks with SVTS, and forms a boundary-aware curriculum by rewarding the Proposer for questions on the Solver's capability boundary.
